rationale: itnet_v2-claude-agentic: itnet_k=1, unet_c=32, itnet_alpha_init=0.0026, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=0.00025, pretrain_epochs=15, pretrain_patience=15, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=600, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=ITER-4 (breast itnet_v2 search-20260703-01, strict 20-min budget). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): k-curve now fully mapped -> hr(k=1)=0.3382, hr(k=2)=0.2098, hr(k=4)=0.0000 (val_ssim 0.9082 / 0.8877 / 0.7636; PSNR 32.28 / 30.55 / 23.73). (2) FINDING: hr is MONOTONE-DECREASING in k -- every extra data-consistency step strictly hurts on breast's 128-view sparse geometry; k=1 is OPTIMAL and is now LOCKED. Remaining FAILURE MODE: at k=1 the recon (PSNR 32.28) still trails the FBP baseline (36.32); iter-2 was effectively the pretrained denoiser + one mild DC step, and the pretrain loss floored at ~1e-6 (train-perfect) while val PSNR is only 32.28 -> a CAPACITY/GENERALIZATION gap in the c=16 SmallUNet denoiser on 512^2 breast detail, not a DC problem. (3) ONE KNOB: unet_c 16 -> 32 (double denoiser width/capacity). ALL else identical to iter-2 (the k=1 champion): itnet_k=1, alpha_init=0.0026, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=2.5e-4, pretrain_epochs=15, patience=15, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=600, val_n=200, seed=42. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if unet_c 16->32, val hr rises above 0.3382 because a wider U-Net has more capacity to model fine breast structure the c=16 net under-fits at eval (train loss was already ~0, so the bottleneck is representational capacity/generalization, not optimization). FALSIFIER: if hr <= ~0.34 (flat or down), c=16 was NOT capacity-limited (the gap is data/regularization or an intrinsic DC-vs-FBP ceiling), and iter-5 pivots to more train data (train_n up) or lower alpha. (5) BUDGET: c=32 ~4x the conv FLOPs of c=16 but the model is tiny (iter-2 params 0.233M at c=16); iter-1 ran c=16/k=4 in 240s, c=32/k=1 is comfortably < 1200s. (6) Loop continues; I dispatch iter-5 myself when iter-4 lands.
